chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yusuf ibn Abi Yaqoub (the rice seller), from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who repents from a sin is like the one who has no sin, and the one who remains steadfast upon the sin while claiming to seek forgiveness from it is like the mocker.'

key_terms.بَيَّاعِ الْأَرُزِّ: The rice seller (a known epithet for Yusuf ibn Abi Yaqoub)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between true repentance and claiming forgiveness while continuing in sin?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish the ontological weight of sincere tawbah, where the sinner is spiritually reinstated to the status of one who never sinned. The hadith further contrasts this with the hypocritical state of those who remain entrenched in their transgressions while merely uttering words of forgiveness, likening them to mockers who lack genuine conviction. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the internal state of the heart over mere verbal declaration.
